syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

topics.title: Mesopotamia: Names, Languages and Early Archaeology
topics.ncert_sections: Introduction

concepts.learning_objective: Recall the names and successive languages of Mesopotamia across its history.
Explain how links with the Old Testament shaped early archaeology in Mesopotamia and how its focus later changed.

topics.title: Mesopotamia and its Geography
topics.ncert_sections: Mesopotamia and its Geography

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the different environments of Iraq and the livelihoods each supported.
Explain how river silt and irrigation made the southern desert highly productive.

topics.title: The Significance of Urbanism and the Movement of Goods
topics.ncert_sections: The Significance of Urbanism; Movement of Goods into Cities

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why division of labour and social organisation are marks of urban life.
Describe what Mesopotamia lacked and how it obtained those resources through trade.
Explain why water transport was vital for the viability of city economies.

topics.title: The Development, System and Uses of Writing
topics.ncert_sections: The Development of Writing; The System of Writing; Literacy; The Uses of Writing

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why writing began in Mesopotamia and what the earliest tablets recorded.
Describe how cuneiform was written and why it was hard to master.
Analyse the extent of literacy and the uses and meanings of writing in Mesopotamia.

topics.title: Urbanisation in Southern Mesopotamia: Temples, Kings and Seals
topics.ncert_sections: Urbanisation in Southern Mesopotamia: Temples and Kings; The Seal - An Urban Artefact

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how the temple grew into the main urban institution.
Analyse how war leaders became kings and how they commanded labour.
Explain how cylinder seals were made and used in city life.

topics.title: Life in the City: Ur, Mari and Abu Salabikh
topics.ncert_sections: Life in the City; A Trading Town in a Pastoral Zone; Excavating Mesopotamian Towns

concepts.learning_objective: Describe family life and the layout of houses and streets at Ur.
Explain the relationship between herders and farmers and the prosperity of Mari.
Explain how modern excavation at Abu Salabikh recovered evidence of daily life.

topics.title: Cities in Mesopotamian Culture and the Legacy of Writing
topics.ncert_sections: Cities in Mesopotamian Culture; The Legacy of Writing; An Early Library; And, an Early Archaeologist!

concepts.learning_objective: Identify Mesopotamian achievements in mathematics, astronomy and the division of time.
Describe how Assurbanipal collected and catalogued the library at Nineveh.
Analyse how the Gilgamesh Epic and Nabonidus show Mesopotamian pride in cities and the past.

topics.title: Sources and the two superpowers: Rome and Iran

concepts.learning_objective: Classify the textual, documentary and material sources used by historians of the Roman Empire.
Describe the extent of the Roman and Iranian empires and the place of the Mediterranean in Rome's empire.

topics.title: The Early Empire

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the roles of the emperor, the Senate and the army in the Principate founded by Augustus.
Explain how cities and provincial upper classes made it possible to govern the vast empire.

topics.title: The Third-Century Crisis

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the external pressures and internal strains that marked the third century.

topics.title: Gender, Literacy, Culture

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the Roman nuclear family and the legal position of women in marriage.
Analyse the evidence for casual literacy and the linguistic and cultural diversity of the empire.

topics.title: Economic Expansion

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how amphorae help archaeologists reconstruct trade in wine and olive oil.
Describe fertile and less developed regions and the technological sophistication of the Roman economy.

topics.title: Controlling Workers

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the place of slave, free and wage labour in the Roman economy.
Describe the methods Roman employers used to supervise and control workers.

topics.title: Social Hierarchies

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the social groups of the early and late empire as described by Tacitus and later sources.
Explain the shift to gold coinage, the affluence of the bureaucracy and the role of Roman law.

topics.title: Late Antiquity

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the state reforms of Diocletian and Constantine, including the solidus and Constantinople.
Analyse the Christianisation of the empire, the post-Roman kingdoms in the West and the rise of Islam.

topics.title: Western Europe after Rome and the feudal order

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the feudal order of lords, vassals and serfs that took shape in western Europe from the ninth century.
Explain the role of the Catholic Church and monasteries in feudal society.

topics.title: Commerce, crusades and the Renaissance

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how Venetian and Genoese trade and the crusades linked Europe with the eastern Mediterranean.
Explain the change in attitudes towards human life that marked the Renaissance.

topics.title: Voyages of discovery and European encounters

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the routes and goals of the European voyages of discovery.
Recognise individuals who connected Europeans with other peoples, such as Leo Africanus and Dona Marina.

topics.title: Encounters seen from both sides

concepts.learning_objective: Analyse the contrasting attitudes Europeans showed towards the peoples they met.
Evaluate how non-Europeans perceived and responded to Europeans and the impact of European diseases.

topics.title: Timeline III (c. 1300 to 1700)

concepts.learning_objective: Place major events of 1300-1700 across Africa, Europe, Asia, South Asia and the Americas in sequence.
Interpret how trade-driven contacts between continents shared ideas and goods but also caused war and displacement.

topics.title: Introduction to Feudalism: France and England
topics.ncert_sections: Introduction, An Introduction to Feudalism, France and England

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the economic, social and political meaning of feudalism in medieval Europe.
Identify the sources used by historians of medieval Europe and Marc Bloch's contribution.
Describe how the Frankish kingdom of France developed close links with the Church.

topics.title: The Three Orders and the Nobility: Vassalage, Manor and Knights
topics.ncert_sections: The Three Orders, The Second Order: The Nobility, The Manorial Estate, The Knights

concepts.learning_objective: State the idea of the three orders of society held by French priests.
Explain vassalage and the privileges enjoyed by the nobility.
Describe the manorial estate and the role of knights and fiefs.

topics.title: The First Order: Clergy, Monks and the Church in Society
topics.ncert_sections: The First Order: The Clergy, Monks, The Church and Society

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the power, income and rules of membership of the Catholic Church and clergy.
Explain the life and functions of monks, nuns and friars in medieval monasteries.
Analyse how Christian practice blended with feudal customs and older folk traditions.

topics.title: The Third Order: Free Peasants, Serfs and Feudalism in England
topics.ncert_sections: The Third Order: Peasants, Free and Unfree; England

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish between the obligations of free peasants and serfs.
Describe how William I established feudalism in England after the Norman Conquest.

topics.title: Factors Affecting Social and Economic Relations: Environment, Land Use and Technology
topics.ncert_sections: Factors Affecting Social and Economic Relations: The Environment, Land Use, New Agricultural Technology

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how climate and forests shaped agriculture in medieval Europe.
Describe primitive land use and the passive resistance of peasants.
Analyse the effects of new agricultural technology and the three-field system.

topics.title: A Fourth Order? Towns, Guilds and Cathedral-towns
topics.ncert_sections: A Fourth Order? New Towns and Townspeople, Cathedral-towns

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why towns grew from the eleventh century and why they attracted serfs.
Describe the role of guilds and the rise of town merchants.
Explain how cathedrals led to the growth of towns and served the people.

topics.title: The Crisis of the Fourteenth Century, Social Unrest and Political Changes
topics.ncert_sections: The Crisis of the Fourteenth Century, Social Unrest, Political Changes, The New Monarchy

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the causes and consequences of the fourteenth-century crisis, including the Black Death.
Explain why peasants revolted and why old feudal relations could not be reimposed.
Evaluate how the new monarchs centralised power and how France and England diverged.

topics.title: The Renaissance Idea and the Revival of Italian Cities
topics.ncert_sections: Introduction; The Revival of Italian Cities

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how Jacob Burckhardt used the term Renaissance to describe a new humanist culture in Italian towns.
Explain why Italian towns revived as independent city-states where the idea of citizenship took root.

topics.title: Universities, Humanism and the Humanist View of History
topics.ncert_sections: Universities and Humanism; The Humanist View of History

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the humanist educational programme associated with Petrarch and the subjects called the humanities.
Explain how Florence became a centre of learning and what the term 'Renaissance Man' means.
Evaluate the humanist division of European history into the Middle Ages and the Modern Age.

topics.title: Science and Philosophy: The Arabs' Contribution
topics.ncert_sections: Science and Philosophy: The Arabs' Contribution

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how Arab translators preserved and transmitted Greek learning to European scholars.
Identify Muslim scholars whose works were valued in the Italian world and their contributions.

topics.title: Artists, Realism and Architecture
topics.ncert_sections: Artists and Realism; Architecture

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how anatomy, geometry and light contributed to realism in Italian art.
Describe the revival of the imperial Roman 'classical' style in Renaissance architecture and its leading figures.

topics.title: Printing and a New Concept of Human Beings
topics.ncert_sections: The First Printed Books; A New Concept of Human Beings

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the printing press helped spread humanist ideas beyond Italy.
Analyse the humanist views of human nature expressed by writers such as Barbaro, Valla and Machiavelli.

topics.title: The Aspirations of Women
topics.ncert_sections: The Aspirations of Women

concepts.learning_objective: Compare the position of women in aristocratic and merchant families in Renaissance Italy.
Assess the contributions of women such as Cassandra Fedele and Isabella d'Este to humanist culture.

topics.title: Debates within Christianity
topics.ncert_sections: Debates within Christianity

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the criticisms Christian humanists made of the Church, including indulgences and the Donation of Constantine.
Describe the Protestant Reformation, its spread, and the Catholic Church's response.

topics.title: The Scientific Revolution and Reconsidering the Renaissance
topics.ncert_sections: The Copernican Revolution; Reading the Universe; Was there a European 'Renaissance' in the Fourteenth Century?

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how Copernicus, Kepler, Galileo and Newton overturned the earth-centred view of the universe.
Describe how the Scientific Revolution separated knowledge from belief and was popularised by scientific societies.
Evaluate the arguments of historians who question Burckhardt's idea of a sharp Renaissance break.

topics.title: Introduction and European Imperialism
topics.ncert_sections: Introduction; European Imperialism

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how European settlement in the Americas, Australia and New Zealand displaced native peoples and how colonies became states.
Distinguish the different forms of control Europeans established in South Asia, Africa and settler colonies.
Describe how native histories came to be written and how native names survive in place-names.

topics.title: The Native Peoples of North America
topics.ncert_sections: North America; The Native Peoples

concepts.learning_objective: Recall when and how the earliest inhabitants reached North America and how their population grew.
Describe the economy, beliefs and customs of the native peoples of North America.

topics.title: Encounters with Europeans and Mutual Perceptions
topics.ncert_sections: Encounters with Europeans; Mutual Perceptions

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the nature of early trade between Europeans and natives and its effects.
Compare the different European views of native Americans, from the 'noble savage' to Jefferson.
Analyse the contrast between native gift exchange and the European idea of commodities.

topics.title: Expansion of the USA and Canada and the Loss of Native Land
topics.ncert_sections: The Native Peoples Lose their Land; The Gold Rush, and the Growth of Industries

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how the USA and Canada expanded and how settlers transformed the land.
Explain how native peoples lost their land through treaties, removal and reservations.
Explain how the Gold Rush, railways and industry changed North America.

topics.title: Constitutional Rights and the Winds of Change in North America
topics.ncert_sections: Constitutional Rights; The Winds of Change

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why the democratic rights and the right to property in the USA excluded natives.
Trace the reforms from the Meriam survey to Canada's Constitution Act of 1982.

topics.title: Australia: Aborigines and European Settlement
topics.ncert_sections: Australia; The Europeans Reach Australia; The Development of Australia

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the origins, diversity and beliefs of Australia's native peoples.
Explain how British penal settlement led to the displacement of the aborigines.
Describe the economic development of Australia and its policy towards non-white labour.

topics.title: Australia: The Winds of Change
topics.ncert_sections: The Winds of Change (Australia)

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how historians and writers challenged the silence about the aborigines.
Evaluate the legal and public steps taken to recognise native land rights and past injustice.

topics.title: Japan under the Tokugawa
topics.ncert_sections: Introduction; Japan: The Political System

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the political organisation of Tokugawa Japan under the shogun, daimyo and samurai.
Explain the economic and intellectual developments before 1868 that prepared Japan for rapid modernisation.

topics.title: The Meiji Restoration
topics.ncert_sections: The Meiji Restoration

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why Commodore Perry's arrival in 1853 led to the restoration of the emperor in 1868.
Describe the Meiji policies of 'fukoku kyohei', the emperor system and the new school system.
Explain how Japan adapted the Chinese script through hiragana and katakana.

topics.title: Modernising the Economy and Aggressive Nationalism
topics.ncert_sections: Modernising the Economy; Industrial Workers; Aggressive Nationalism

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the steps the Meiji government took to modernise the Japanese economy.
Analyse the character of Japan's industrial workforce and the environmental cost of rapid industrialisation.
Explain how the military gained independent power under the Meiji constitution.

topics.title: Westernisation, Daily Life and Post-war Japan
topics.ncert_sections: 'Westernisation' and 'Tradition'; Daily Life; 'Overcoming Modernity'; After Defeat: Re-emerging as a Global Economic Power

concepts.learning_objective: Compare the views of Fukuzawa Yukichi, Miyake Setsurei and Ueki Emori on Japan's relationship with the West.
Describe how family life and urban culture in Japan changed with modernisation.
Explain the reforms of the US-led Occupation and the reasons for Japan's post-war economic recovery.

topics.title: China: From the Qing to the Guomindang
topics.ncert_sections: China; The Opium Trade; The Examination System; Establishing the Republic

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the opium trade and the Opium War undermined the Qing and how reformers responded.
Explain why the Chinese examination system was abolished in 1905.
Describe Sun Yat-sen's Three Principles and evaluate why the Guomindang failed.

topics.title: The Communist Party and the People's Republic of China
topics.ncert_sections: The Rise of the Communist Party of China; Establishing the New Democracy: 1949-65; Conflicting Visions: 1965-78; Reforms from 1978; The Story of Taiwan

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how Mao Zedong's peasant-based strategy helped the CCP win power.
Describe the policies of the People's Republic from the New Democracy to the Cultural Revolution and the 1978 reforms.
Describe the political and economic development of Taiwan after 1949.

topics.title: The Story of Korea and Two Roads to Modernisation
topics.ncert_sections: The Story of Korea; Two Roads to Modernisation

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how state-led, export-oriented policies produced rapid economic growth in South Korea.
Trace the struggles that led South Korea from military rule to democracy.
Compare the Japanese and Chinese paths to modernisation.
